solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: This is one party game (6)

blocks.note: the sentence you are reading is itself one of these

annotation.surface: Someone at a gathering points out the game about to be played.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue talks about itself: 'This is one' asks what the sentence you are reading is. 'party game' reads as one phrase, but 'party' belongs to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Cluedo is the board game of solving a country-house murder.

entries.clue: Theatrical appearance announced in holiday venue (8)

indicatorNotes.announced: what is announced is spoken, so we take a word by its sound

blocks.note: a sight = an appearance; said out loud it is SITE

annotation.surface: A showy performer makes an entrance at a holiday resort.
annotation.walkthrough: 'announced' applies only to 'appearance': CAMP is taken as written.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: a campsite is where people pitch tents or park caravans on holiday.

entries.clue: Thugs rip out fixtures in football stadium (8)

indicatorNotes.out: out = wrong, unsettled, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Hooligans tear the fittings out of a football ground.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'rip out' as a phrasal verb, but 'rip' is fodder and 'out' alone signals the rearrangement.
annotation.definitionFit: Uprights are the goalposts, fixed in place at each end of the pitch.

entries.clue: Oddly pretend retiring is difficult (4)

indicatorNotes.retiring: retiring = withdrawing, going backwards, so the letters are reversed

annotation.surface: Someone claims that pretending to be shy is hard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'retiring' looks like 'shy' in the surface, but it tells you to turn PEED round.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: a deep book or thought is profound and so hard to grasp.

entries.clue: A family briefly entertains throng in evening entertainment (5-3)

indicatorNotes.briefly: cut short: KIN loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.entertains: to entertain guests is to take them in, so A…KI holds the next piece

blocks.note: KIN = family, missing its last letter
a press = a crowd, a throng

annotation.surface: A family hosts a crowd at an evening party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'entertains' is at home in a party surface, which hides its job as a container signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Après-ski is the socialising that follows a day on the slopes, usually in the evening.

entries.clue: Musical gift – something a groundskeeper wants (7,5)

blocks.note: the ability to name a note by ear

annotation.walkthrough: In the second sense, a pitch is a sports field, which a groundskeeper tends and wants in perfect shape.
annotation.definitionFit: Perfect pitch is the rare gift of identifying or singing any note without a reference.

entries.clue: Bring back less fine cut (4)

indicatorNotes.less: less = without, so F is taken away

blocks.note: to fetch = to go and bring back
f = fine, as on pencil leads

annotation.surface: An order to restore a smaller fine that was reduced.
annotation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like it wants letters reversed, but 'Bring back' is one phrase meaning FETCH.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: etching cuts lines into metal or glass.

entries.clue: Abruptly stole a black sacred symbol (6)

indicatorNotes.Abruptly: cut off suddenly, so SCARF loses its last letter

blocks.note: a stole is a scarf; SCARF without its last letter

annotation.surface: A thief suddenly snatched a dark religious emblem.
annotation.walkthrough: 'stole' reads as a verb, but it is the noun: a shawl or scarf.
annotation.definitionFit: The scarab beetle was a sacred symbol of rebirth in ancient Egypt.

entries.clue: Confidential note removed for prisoner (6)

indicatorNotes.removed: something removed is taken away, so the note's letters come out of the longer word

blocks.note: ti (te) is a note of the sol-fa scale

annotation.surface: A secret memo has been taken away from someone in jail.
annotation.walkthrough: 'note' suggests a written message, but it is the musical note TI, cut from the middle of INTIMATE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an inmate is someone held in a prison.

entries.clue: After revolution, leftist with spirit crows (6)

annotation.definitionNote: a murder is the collective noun for a group of crows

indicatorNotes.After revolution: turned round, so the joined pieces are reversed

blocks.note: a red = a communist, a leftist

annotation.surface: Following an uprising, a radical drinker boasts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'crows' looks like a verb (boasts), but it is the birds: a flock of crows is a murder.
annotation.definitionFit: 'A murder of crows' is the traditional collective term.

entries.clue: Scottish musicians abandoning the Queen’s state (8)

indicatorNotes.abandoning: leaving behind, so ER'S is dropped

blocks.note: a Scottish pop duo of twin brothers, known for 'I'm Gonna Be (500 Miles)'
ER = the Queen, plus the S of the possessive

annotation.surface: A band from Scotland leaves the Queen's realm.
annotation.walkthrough: The band is The Proclaimers. 'state' looks like a country but is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to state something formally or publicly.

entries.clue: On the other hand, aircrew is not scrambled (12)

indicatorNotes.scrambled: mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Despite expectations, the aircrew has not been sent up in a hurry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'scrambled' is the word for fighter pilots launching in a hurry, so it sits naturally beside 'aircrew'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, the adverb for introducing the opposite view; Tweedledee's favourite word.

entries.clue: Advanced talk about Beowulf? (4)

indicatorNotes.about: round about, so the joined pieces are turned back to front

annotation.surface: A scholar gives an advanced lecture on the Old English poem.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Beowulf as one example of a saga, a long heroic tale.
annotation.definitionFit: Beowulf is a long heroic narrative poem, a saga.

entries.clue: Sky viewer might see this policeman, not entirely satisfied (5)

indicatorNotes.not entirely: incomplete, so COP loses its last letter

blocks.note: met = satisfied, as in 'met the demand'

annotation.surface: A stargazer spots a police officer who is not quite content.
annotation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' seems to qualify 'satisfied', but it cuts short the policeman.
annotation.definitionFit: A comet is something a person looking at the night sky may see.

entries.clue: Scientist has question for the audience (4)

indicatorNotes.for the audience: an audience hears it, so the word is taken by sound

annotation.surface: A researcher takes questions from the people listening.
annotation.walkthrough: James Watt was the Scottish engineer whose steam engine improvements drove the Industrial Revolution.
annotation.definitionFit: James Watt was an eighteenth-century scientist and inventor.

entries.clue: Sylvester Stallone regularly plays in an artful way (5)

indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so every other letter

annotation.surface: The action star always acts with cunning.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole name 'Sylvester Stallone' gives SLY; it is not a source of letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: artful here means crafty, cunning.

entries.clue: Minions stealing left shoes (5)

indicatorNotes.stealing: taking something into their possession, so COGS holds L

blocks.note: a cog in the machine is an unimportant underling

annotation.surface: Little servants make off with someone's footwear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'left' reads as 'abandoned', but it is simply L.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: clogs are one kind of shoe, with wooden soles.

entries.clue: Rumour three times included by headline story (6-6)

indicatorNotes.included by: the Ts are put inside the other words

blocks.note: a title is a headline; one T goes in: TI(T)TLE
a tale is a story; two Ts go in: TA(TT)LE

annotation.surface: Gossip is repeated three times in a lead news story.
annotation.walkthrough: The three Ts are shared out: one into TITLE, two into TALE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean idle gossip passed from person to person.

entries.clue: It’s unimportant talk about order (2,6)

indicatorNotes.about: going round, so NATTER surrounds OM

blocks.note: OM = Order of Merit, a British honour

annotation.surface: Someone dismisses chatter about rank as trivial.
annotation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is an honour given personally by the British monarch.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'no matter' is the brush-off said when something is not worth worrying about.

entries.clue: See Lulu playing, holding Kelvin’s instruments (8)

indicatorNotes.playing: in play, moving about, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: K = kelvin, the unit of temperature

annotation.surface: Go and watch the singer Lulu perform, with Kelvin's guitars.
annotation.walkthrough: Lulu is a Scottish pop singer; 'playing' suits her, but it is an anagram signal. The rearranged letters U(K)ULELES take K after the first U.
annotation.definitionFit: Ukuleles are small four-stringed guitars.

entries.clue: Suggesting plant and equipment for a marina (8,4)

blocks.note: to float an idea is to suggest it

annotation.surface: Someone recommends the machinery and gear a harbour needs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'plant' reads as industrial machinery beside 'equipment', but it is the weed.
annotation.definitionFit: A floating dock is a buoyant platform used in marinas to berth and lift boats.

entries.clue: Fearful catching wife standing up for fool (6)

indicatorNotes.catching: to catch something is to trap it, so the fearful word closes round the wife
indicatorNotes.standing up: in a down entry, standing up means reading from the bottom, so it is reversed

annotation.surface: A nervous husband, grabbing his wife, defends an idiot.
annotation.walkthrough: W goes after TI: TI(W)MID, then the whole reads upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both name a slow-witted person.

entries.clue: Feature about gold showing one way to obtain money (6)

blocks.note: the brow is a facial feature

annotation.surface: A newspaper article on gold explains a way to raise cash.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Feature' suggests a magazine article, but it is part of the face.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose description: taking a loan is one of several routes to cash, alongside earning or stealing.

entries.clue: I study picture (4)

blocks.note: to con = to study, learn by heart

annotation.surface: Someone examines a painting.
annotation.walkthrough: CON meaning to study is an old usage kept alive by crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: An icon is a picture, especially a religious image.

entries.clue: Nick some salt (5)

blocks.note: to nick = to steal, British slang
as much salt as fits between finger and thumb

annotation.surface: Steal a little salt from the table.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nick' is a verb, not a name: a pinch of salt is the small amount, and to pinch is to steal.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: to steal, and a tiny amount held between the fingers.

entries.clue: Consumed flipping large Indian dish (4)

indicatorNotes.flipping: flipped over, so HAD is turned round

blocks.note: l = large, as on clothes labels

annotation.surface: Someone wolfed down an enormous curry, flipping it over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'flipping' could be a mild British swear word here, but it reverses HAD.
annotation.definitionFit: Dahl (dal) is an Indian dish of spiced lentils.

entries.clue: Tips of some asparagus going on starchy food (4)

indicatorNotes.Tips of: the tips are the ends, here the first letters

annotation.surface: Asparagus spears are served on a bed of starch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'on' looks like a link word joining the parts, but it supplies the final O.
annotation.definitionFit: Sago is a starch from palm pith, used in puddings.

entries.clue: Letter to the Corinthians kept back by conservatoire (4)

indicatorNotes.kept: something kept by a word is held within it, so the answer lies inside 'conservatoire'
indicatorNotes.back: going back means travelling the wrong way, so the letters run right to left

annotation.surface: A letter to the church in Corinth is held back by a music school.
annotation.walkthrough: The Corinthians spoke Greek, so their letters were Greek letters; the surface pretends it is Paul's epistle.
annotation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet.

entries.clue: Poison of interminable fighting (8)

indicatorNotes.interminable: without its end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: warfaring = waging war, fighting; the final G is cut

annotation.surface: Endless conflict is described as toxic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'interminable' means endless in the surface and literally no end: WARFARING loses its G.
annotation.definitionFit: Warfarin is a rat poison, also used in small doses as a blood thinner.

entries.clue: Place to stay with the Spanish army at the front (6)

indicatorNotes.at the front: the army goes before the Spanish word

annotation.surface: A billet with the Spanish forces on the front line.
annotation.walkthrough: 'at the front' sounds like the battlefront, but it puts HOST first.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: youth hostels offer cheap dormitory beds to travellers.

entries.clue: Lines of Oscar Wilde originally found in figures of speech (3,5)

indicatorNotes.originally: at the origin, the start, so each word gives its first letter
indicatorNotes.found in: something found in a place sits inside it, so OW goes inside TROPES

blocks.note: first letters of Oscar and Wilde

annotation.surface: Quotations from Oscar Wilde turn up in lists of rhetorical devices.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lines' looks like lines of verse, but it means ropes. T(OW)ROPES.
annotation.definitionFit: Tow ropes are lines used to pull vehicles or boats.

entries.clue: Grave markers in Australian city (6)

blocks.note: piles of stones over a burial

annotation.surface: Tombstones in an Australian town.
annotation.walkthrough: Cairns is a city in far north Queensland, gateway to the Great Barrier Reef.
annotation.definitionFit: Cairns are mounds of stones, often raised as grave markers.
